definition: Ann Alicia Copestake is professor of computational linguistics and head of the Department of Computer Science and Technology at the University of Cambridge and a fellow of Wolfson College, Cambridge.
details: Ann Alicia Copestake is professor of computational linguistics and head of the Department of Computer Science and Technology at the University of Cambridge and a fellow of Wolfson College, Cambridge.

explainer.lead: Ann Copestake is a computational linguistics researcher whose work explores how computers can represent and interpret human language. She is a professor and head of the Department of Computer Science and Technology at the University of Cambridge, and her research includes word meaning, grammar, and named-entity recognition.

tiers.eli5: Ann Copestake studies how computers can make sense of human language. Think of the word “bank”: it could mean a place that keeps money or the land beside a river, and a computer needs clues to choose the right meaning. Her research includes problems like this, along with phrases whose meaning comes from several words together.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers working on language systems encounter problems addressed by Copestake’s research, including ambiguous word senses, multiword expressions, named entities, and grammatical representations. This is research background rather than a ready-made library or model; implementation and evaluation choices depend on the particular publication and task.
tiers.paperLevel: Copestake’s research spans computational linguistics and natural language processing, including minimal recursion semantics, feature structure grammars, lexical semantics, polysemy, multiword expressions, and named-entity recognition. Her 1992 PhD at the University of Sussex concerned lexical semantics and was supervised by Gerald Gazdar.

usedIn.name: Computational linguistics

usedIn.name: Natural language processing
usedIn.detail: She began research in this field at Cambridge in 1985 and has published on named-entity recognition and multiword expressions.

usedIn.name: Lexical semantics

explainer.knownFor: Copestake is known for research in computational linguistics and natural language processing, particularly minimal recursion semantics, multiword expressions, polysemy, named-entity recognition, and feature structure grammars. She also holds senior academic roles at the University of Cambridge.
